title: Remove Duplicate Characters
directAnswer: Keep a 'seen' set; for each character, if it isn't in the set, append it and add it. O(n) time, O(k) space.

remember.takeaway: First-occurrence-only = a seen set plus a builder.
remember.formula: seen=set(); for ch: if ch not in seen: seen.add(ch); out+=ch

problemStatement: Given a string `s`, return a new string keeping only the first occurrence of each character, preserving order.
understanding: Track which characters you've already emitted in a set; append a character only the first time you see it.

approaches.name: Seen set build
approaches.whenToMention: This is the standard, expected solution — lead with it.
approaches.explanation:
Keep only the first occurrence of each character: track a **seen set** and append a character to the output only the first time you encounter it. Combines the seen-set membership pattern with a filtered build.

**Why a set preserves order.** You scan left to right and append on first sighting, so the kept characters appear in their original order — no sorting. Later repeats fail the membership test and are skipped.

**The Java idiom `seen.add(ch)`.** `Set.add` returns true only when the element was newly added, so `if (seen.add(ch)) sb.append(ch);` both records and filters in one line.

**Performance.** Use a StringBuilder, not `+=`, to keep the build O(n). The set gives O(1) membership, so the whole thing is O(n) time, O(k) space.
hints: What structure tells you 'have I already kept this char?'
Append only on first sighting to preserve order.
Use a StringBuilder; `set.add` returns true only when newly added.
approaches.complexityReasoning: O(1) set lookup and append per character; the set holds k ≤ alphabet-size keys.

java.explanation: add returns true only the first time — append exactly once per char.

patternNote: A core fresher pattern: Seen-set filtered build. Master it on small inputs and it transfers to harder problems.
